title: Catalyzed Multi-Site Proton-Coupled Electron Transfer: Enabling New Amination Reactions
text:
N-N bonds are found across a large range of biologically important molecules including piperazic acid, a non-
ribosomal peptide building block, and FDA-approved drugs such as Cilazapril, an angiotensin-converting enzyme
inhibitor. However, N-N bonds are rarely targeted for strategic synthetic approaches because of the limited
toolset for N-N bond formation and as a result, N-N containing molecule synthesis often relies on using potentially
toxic and dangerous hydrazine or hydroxylamine reagents. The objective of this proposal is to design a general
strategy for accessing reactive nitrogen intermediates from amines to directly form N-N bonds and bioactive
heterocycles, giving synthetic chemists new access to diverse molecular building blocks that will ultimately aid
in widespread distribution of new drug-like architectures to the biomedical community.

title: Northwestern University O'Brien Kidney National Resource Center
text:
Kidney diseases affect 37 million people in the United States. Despite recent advances in treatment options,
there remains an urgent unmet need to identify new therapeutic targets and treatments to bend the arc of kidney
diseases and reduce these staggering numbers. The Northwestern University National Resource Core
Center (NU-NRC) will harness the power of the physical sciences to provide innovative platforms, new
approaches and reagents to kidney researchers to enable new solutions and find cures.

title: Cardiac regulation of heart failure and obesity
text:
MTCH2 is a mitochondrial protein that can have genetic changes that associate with cardiac disease and
obesity in humans. Removing Mtch2 from the heart causes the heart to malfunction and leads to loss of body
weight in mice. This study will uncover how MTCH2 function is critical for the heart and obesity.

title: Next-Generation Algorithms in Statistical Genetics Based on Modern Machine Learning
text:
This proposal aims to develop next-generation algorithms for statistical genetics based on
modern machine learning, focusing on three broad areas: modeling linkage disequilibrium and
the structure of genetic variation, analyzing genome-wide association study data, and predicting
risk from genetic and environmental factors. Within in each area, we aim to develop open-
source systems for key applied problems including genetic imputation, haplotyping, low-pass
sequencing, causal variant identification, and risk scoring. By leveraging massive data, our
methods will help reveal novel genetic factors that influence disease; improve the accuracy of
genomic prediction in domains from preventive medicine to pharmacogenomics; significantly
reduce the cost of genomic sequencing assays; and ultimately improve human health.

title: Extended amygdala somatostatin role in post-traumatic stress and alcohol use disorder
text:
Post-traumatic stress and alcohol use disorder (PTSD/AUD) are frequently comorbid and are a major public
health problem. The proposed multidisciplinary research is relevant to the mission of NIAAA and addresses
important gaps in the literature on examining the role of antistress neurocircuitry (somatostatin) underlying
PTSD/AUD comorbidity and novel mechanistic strategies for their prevention and treatment.

title: Role of transposon regulation in the negligible senescence of S. mediterranea
text:
With age, most stem cells lose their ability to adequately replace damaged tissue cells and respond to tissue
regenerative needs, but the causes of this loss in potency remain unclear. Goal of this project is to use the
negligibly senescent planarian stem cell system to identify the role of transposon silencing and chromatin
maintenance in their ability to avoid age-related changes. This project will contribute to a better understanding
of the biology of aging, and to the identification of new strategies to improve the human health span.

title: Genomic and metabolomic foundations of human-microbial symbiosis in the gut
text:
A central premise of this project is that healthy growth of infants and children requires coordinated
development of our human organs and of the large community of microbes that inhabit our intestines (the `gut
microbiota'). We have (i) found that children with undernutrition - a devastating, pervasive global health
challenge - have impaired development of their gut microbial communities, and (ii) developed a microbiota-
directed therapeutic food formulation that, in randomized controlled clinical trials conducted in Bangladesh
involving 12-18-month undernourished children, repaired their microbiota and produced greater improvements
in ponderal and linear growth than a standard nutritional supplement, even though the microbiota-directed food
had fewer calories. This project builds on these findings. It describes an approach for marrying microbiome
science and human nutrition to select glycan components harvested from the byproduct streams of food
manufacture as prebiotics that are able to effectively target a key growth-promoting member of the developing
microbiota - one that exhibits strain-level diversity within and between populations. Identifying the bioactive
components of a food and characterizing their interactions with their microbial targets has therapeutic
implications including (i) improved efficacy based on better knowledge of dosing, (ii) use of prebiotic
formulations in lieu of the need to manufacture and distribute shelf-stable therapeutic food formulations; (iii)
use of synbiotics (prebiotic and probiotic formulations consisting of the glycans plus their targeted bacterial
strains) to treat children who initially fail to respond to treatment with microbiota-directed therapeutic foods
and/or lack responsive strains. It also has implications for disease prevention including development of
recommendations about the types of complementary foods that should be administered to weaning-age
children to ensure healthy development of their gut microbiota.

title: Point of Care Technologies for Nutrition, Infection, and Cancer for Global Health (PORTENT)
text:
Point-of-care zinc supplement quality verification is limited by expensive laboratory
requirements ($65+, multi-day delays), compromising therapeutic efficacy where zinc deficiency
causes 450,000+ annual deaths. Novel zinc-specific fluorescent probe technology with
smartphone analysis enables instant supplement quality verification at <$1. This approach could
revolutionize clinical decision-making and patient care.

title: Next-generation imaging to interrogate biological systems across time and space
text:
RELEVANCE TO PUBLIC HEALTH
The proposed research will develop new microscopes to better observe biological specimens and will use new
imaging techniques to understand how protein diffusion, epigenetic modifications, and chromatin work together
to orchestrate diverse biological functions in the cell nucleus.

title: iPSC-derived retina
text:
Retinal diseases are a major cause of vision impairment and irreversible blindness. The availability of a human retina cell
model will enable the study of retinal disease in patients own cells and serve as a resource for cell-based therapy.
Therefore, in this proposal, we will use human cells and state-of art bioengineering approaches to develop human retina
tissue for future use in disease modeling, drug screening, and transplantation studies.

title: Training Program in NeuroHIV (TPNH)
text:
This research training program is focused on the scientific and professional development of
advanced predoctoral thesis students in the area of neuronal degeneration caused by Human
Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV). Through didactic coursework, laboratory research, career
development training, this program will create a core of scientists who will contribute to the
understanding, treatment and prevention of HIV-associated neuronal disorders.

title: Functional genomic dissection of lung cancer in vivo
text:
We will use highly quantitative autochthonous mouse model systems and somatic genome editing to uncover all
lung cancer tumor suppressors and determine the extent to which genomic context defines tumor suppressor
gene function. Uncovering the global gene expression states induced by defined combinatorial genomic
alterations, will provide further insights into the molecular determinants of tumor suppression and lung cancer
growth in vivo.

title: PG4AD: Scaling up pangenome graph for genotyping complex structural variations for Alzheimer's disease genetics
text:
The uptake and utilization of the HPRC pangenome resources is limited by the lack of efficient tools for
analyzing complex structural variations (SVs) at the population level over the pangenome graph. We will
develop new path-based pangenome graph-native methods and tools for SV detection and imputation, and
apply them to analyze Alzheimer’s disease sequencing project (ADSP) data. Our project will broaden the
adoption of HPRC resources and empower the human genetics and AD research community.

title: Biology and structure of pMHC receptors functioning as mechanosensors in the [alpha][beta] T-cell lineage
text:
T lymphocytes recognize host cells altered by infections or cancer-causing transformations using force
applied to their surface T cell receptors to tune both cellular detection acuity and differentiation. Forces arise
from T-cell motions locally (internally) or as T cells traffic through the host tissues (externally). By characterizing
these force-dependent processes, we shall be able to understand and ultimately manipulate T-cell activation and
memory inducing rapid recall responses, fostering protective immunity and improving immunotherapies via
rational synthetic biology.

title: Dynamics of activity-induced transcription in single dentate granule cells
text:
To navigate daily life, novel experiences must constantly be compared to prior experiences to determine
whether prior information is still accurate or if conditions have changed. This project will link novel-experience-
induced changes in individual neurons of the dentate gyrus, which is critical for distinguishing between similar
experiences, to physiological states in which memory function is enhanced or impaired. Understanding the link
between gene expression in individual cells and memory function will reveal novel targets for maintaining
healthy memory and restoring function in aging and disease.

title: In-Situ Generation of Dual TCR/CAR T Cells for Immunotherapy with Lipid Nanoparticles
text:
This study will develop and validate a lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-based platform to activate and
transfect CD4+ T cells, characterize antigen-presenting molecules, and assess the functionality and
efficacy of engineered CD4+ CAR-T cells in treating tumors in vivo.

title: Modeling Epstein-Barr Virus Germinal Center Infection with Tonsil Organoids
text:
As an orally transmitted pathogen, EBV establishes lifelong infection of tonsils, where it can alter B lymphocyte
development, growth and survival and their interactions with other tonsil cells. This research aims to utilize a
new tonsil organoid model to investigate how EBV establishes persistent infection, including by evading the
immune system to cause disease. Insights gained could lead to new therapeutic strategies for treating EBV-
driven conditions, including cancer and autoimmune diseases, thereby enhancing public health.

title: Core B: Tissue, Histology and Imaging Core
text:
The Tissue/Histology/Imaging Core (Core B) is critical for achieving the goals of the UPMC Hillman 
Cancer Center Head and Neck (HN) SPORE by acquiring and storing biospecimen and patient imaging, 
processing both and performing of a large variety of cutting-edge analysis techniques to support all HN 
SPORE projects.

title: Maternal Obstetric Monitoring System (MOMS): a Postpartum Hemorrhage (PPH) Wearable Monitor
text:
This research introduces the Maternal Obstetrics Monitoring System (MOMS), a technology
designed to improve early detection of postpartum hemorrhage (PPH), a leading cause of
maternal death. By continuously monitoring vital signs and performing advanced analysis of the
measurements, MOMS aims to identify significant blood loss in new mothers more effectively,
potentially enhancing maternal health and reducing fatalities from PPH.

title: Unraveling human intervertebral disc development with stem cells
text:
Degeneration of the intervertebral disc (IVD) causes limited motility and chronic pain, yet there are no
effective treatments due to a lack of understanding of the IVD. We aim to advance IVD biology from the
perspective of human spinal development. We use human pluripotent stem cells to recapitulate IVD
development in the dish and elucidate multi-scale mechanisms of human IVD formation.
